title: Mozzarella sticks, breaded, baked or fried

content.title: About
content.content: Mozzarella sticks are cheese sticks coated in seasoned breadcrumbs and cooked either in the oven or deep‑fried. They feature a golden, crunchy crust and a warm, stretchy mozzarella core.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mozzarella sticks are a staple appetizer in many American fast‑food restaurants.
They are traditionally made from whole mozzarella blocks cut into 1–2 cm thick strips.
The breading often includes a mix of breadcrumbs, spices, and sometimes grated Parmesan.
Baked versions are lower in calories but still retain the characteristic crunch.
In some regions they are called “mozzarella sticks” or “mozzarella croquettes.”

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Mozzarella provides a good amount of calcium, essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: The cheese supplies complete protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Mozzarella contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic potential
items.content: Certain mozzarella varieties contain live cultures that may benefit gut microbiota.

items.title: Low sugar
items.content: Unlike many snack foods, mozzarella sticks contain virtually no sugar.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to dairy or lactose may experience reactions.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Fried sticks are rich in saturated fat and calories, so they should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: The breading is often salty; those monitoring sodium intake should choose a low‑salt version.

items.title: Trans fats in processed versions
items.content: Some commercial products may contain trans fats, which are detrimental to heart health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve mozzarella sticks hot with dipping sauces such as marinara, cheese sauce, ranch, or honey‑mustard. They are convenient as a finger food appetizer or can be added to salads and pasta dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked sticks in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Frozen sticks last up to 2 months; reheat in the oven or microwave before serving.
